To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

‘A healthy diet, including a high consumption of fruit, vegetables and fatty fish, and low consumption of trans fatty acids, may take away 20-30 per cent of the burden of chronic diseases, and add approximately one year to life expectancy’.
a healthy diet may prevent a considerable amount of cardiovascular disease.

the burden of cardiovascular diseases in the Dutch population can be reduced by 20-30%, by adherence to recommendations for fruit, vegetables and fatty acids, with a gain of approximately half a year of life expectancy for a person aged 40 years.

the burden of disease and the potential benefits that could be achieved by a change in dietary habits.
the burden of chronic disease in the Netherlands.
the development, validation, and application of a computer model to quantify the burden and cost of chronic diseases in the Netherlands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(i) a diet low in saturated and trans fatty acid and high in fruit and vegetables and fish is associated with lower risk for coronary heart disease and stroke; (ii) a diet low is saturated and trans fatty-acid and high in fruit, vegetables and fibre is associated with lower blood cholesterol levels; (iii) a diet high in fruit and fibre is associated in lower blood pressure; (iv) a diet high is fish is associated with higher intake of n-3 fatty acids;
the consumption of fruit, vegetables and oily fish is associated with a reduction in the risk of CHD and stroke.

a healthy diet can prevent cardiovascular disease, and that the benefits can be large.
a healthy diet is the best prevention for cardiovascular disease.
a healthy diet can reduce the burden of cardiovascular diseases and increase life expectancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a healthy diet is an important part of the prevention of cardiovascular diseases and can reduce the burden of cardiovascular diseases.
a diet rich in fruit, vegetables, and fish and with low saturated and trans fatty acid levels can substantially reduce the burden of cardiovascular diseases.
the impact of dietary factors on the prevention of cardiovascular diseases is much larger than previously thought.
